title: PNP says no major threats monitored ahead of Trump's arrival for ASEAN Summit
summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said Tuesday that it has not monitored any major security threats ahead of the arrival of United States President Donald Trump for the 49th ASEAN Summit.

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said Tuesday that it has not monitored any major security threats ahead of the arrival of United States President Donald Trump for the 49th ASEAN Summit.
At a press briefing, PNP spokesperson Police Brigadier General Allen Rae Co said the security situation remained generally peaceful despite tensions between cops and protesters.
"No major threats na namo-monitor. But of course, we are monitoring and constantly surveying 'yung situation," Co said.
The PNP said security arrangements were already in place for all summit activities and visiting foreign dignitaries, including Trump.
Asked whether additional security personnel would be deployed for Trump's arrival, Co said authorities were confident that the existing security preparations would be sufficient.
The PNP reiterated their warning to protesters planning to stage demonstrations against the US leader and the Pax Silica initiative.
According to the police, protesters should limit their activities to designated freedom parks and warned that authorities would make arrests if they violate existing laws.
Co said authorities would not allow protesters to march toward the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), where ASEAN Summit activities are being held. —AOL, GMA News
